# Review Dependabot PRs

> **Skill version:** 1.1 · see [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).

Fold the open Dependabot pull requests into **one of them**, whose body carries per-package evidence, so a human approves once instead of N times and knows what was actually checked. The other bumps land as commits on that PR's branch; no new branch and no new PR are created.

Two things make a bump-by-bump merge the wrong shape here:

- **Every uv bump edits the same `requires-dist` block in `uv.lock`.** Merge them one at a time and the first lands while the rest come back as conflicts.
- **A green test run is not evidence for most of these packages.** `ddtrace` patches libraries at import with nothing of ours importing it, `certifi` is the trust store behind every vendor TLS handshake with no import at all, and `aws-cdk-lib` drift shows up at deploy rather than at merge. A generic "it imports, tests pass" checklist produces a generic answer for all three.

So the work is: enumerate, classify by blast radius, gather the evidence that class demands, fold every surviving bump onto one host Dependabot branch, and rewrite that PR's title and body around the evidence.

## Scope

- **pokedex only.** Both of its ecosystems are in scope: the `uv` bumps (`pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock`) and pokedex's own npm entries (`package.json`, no lockfile committed).
- **The sibling repos are out of scope.** eevvee, pokecenter and oak are npm projects; their packages are published as tarballs rather than wheels, so the source-diff technique below needs a different fetch step that this version does not define. Handle their Dependabot queues by hand.

## What this skill never does

- **Never merges, and never ticks a ship-on-merge box.** An approving review is required before anything lands, and the person who merges is the one who decides whether it deploys. The end state is the host PR updated and ready for a human.
- **Never closes the superseded Dependabot PRs.** Name them in the host PR's body so a human closes them when it merges.
- **Never force-pushes, rebases, or amends a Dependabot branch.** Commits are added to it, nothing is rewritten.
- **Never hand-edits `uv.lock`.** Versions are set in `pyproject.toml` and the lockfile is regenerated with `uv lock`.

## Blast-radius classes

Every bump gets exactly one class **before** any evidence is gathered. The class sets the evidence bar; the per-package specifics are in [reference/package-playbooks.md](reference/package-playbooks.md).

| Class | Examples here | What can break | Evidence that settles it |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Silent-runtime** | `ddtrace`, `datadog`, `datadog-lambda` | The package patches or wraps things at import time with no call of ours to grep for, so nothing fails loudly | Check the patching surface against the libraries actually run, plus any private API the code reaches into. A clean import proves nothing |
| **Trust-anchor** | `certifi`, `pycryptodome`, `cryptography` | A dropped CA root or changed cipher default fails every vendor TLS handshake, or leaves stored credentials undecryptable | Diff the trust bundle or the primitive in use, name what was added and removed, and resolve the named consumers |
| **Contract** | `svix`, `apiflask`, `stagehand`, `boto3`, `paramiko`, `serverless-wsgi` | A signature, param shape, or negotiated protocol changes and the caller silently gets less | Read the changed surface in both versions against every call site, naming the file and line |
| **Infrastructure** | `aws-cdk-lib`, `datadog-cdk-constructs-v2` | Template drift lands at deploy time, not merge time: logical-ID churn or resource replacement | `yarn synth` on both versions, diff all rendered templates with sorted keys |
| **Leaf** | `faker`, `ruff`, `pytest-*`, `curlify` | Test, tooling, or local-only surface | Import check plus `yarn test nonints` |

When a package fits two classes, take the stricter one. When it fits none of them, treat it as Contract and say in the PR body why.

## The decisive technique: diff the package source

**Mandatory for every non-leaf bump.** Release notes describe what the maintainer thought was notable; the diff is what shipped.

For a uv package, fetch both wheels:

```bash
rm -rf /tmp/dep-old /tmp/dep-new && mkdir -p /tmp/dep-old /tmp/dep-new
uv pip install --target /tmp/dep-old --no-deps --quiet <package>==<old-version>
uv pip install --target /tmp/dep-new --no-deps --quiet <package>==<new-version>
diff -ru /tmp/dep-old /tmp/dep-new | head -200
```

For an npm package, fetch and unpack both tarballs instead:

```bash
rm -rf /tmp/dep-old /tmp/dep-new && mkdir -p /tmp/dep-old /tmp/dep-new
npm pack <package>@<old-version> --pack-destination /tmp/dep-old --silent
npm pack <package>@<new-version> --pack-destination /tmp/dep-new --silent
for side in old new; do tar -xzf /tmp/dep-$side/*.tgz -C /tmp/dep-$side; done
diff -ru /tmp/dep-old/package /tmp/dep-new/package | head -200
```

Read the diff, then answer only the question the class asks. Two outcomes it produces that release notes cannot:

- A bump can be **provably inert**: if the whole diff across two releases is the `__version__` string, there is nothing left to check.
- A bump that **does** change code can still be provably safe at the call sites: diff the declared names in each changed module and show nothing the code calls was removed or renamed.

Full mechanics, including how to compare declared names and what to do when the diff is large: [workflows/vet.md](workflows/vet.md).

## Phases

| Phase | What | Workflow |
|---|---|---|
| 0 — Inventory | Enumerate the open Dependabot PRs, group by package, drop the ones already superseded on `main` | [workflows/inventory.md](workflows/inventory.md) |
| 1 — Vet | Classify each bump, then run the class's evidence loop and record a verdict line | [workflows/vet.md](workflows/vet.md) |
| 2 — Combine + ship | Pick the host Dependabot PR, add one commit per remaining package, regenerate the lockfile, verify, push to its branch, rewrite its title and body | [workflows/combine-and-ship.md](workflows/combine-and-ship.md) |

Persist the inventory to `.claude/tmp/dependabot-{date}.md` and update each row as it moves through the phases; a queue of five or more bumps usually spans a context window.

## Hard rules

- **Verify every claim against a fresh `origin/main`, not the working tree.** Run `git fetch origin main` and read call sites at that commit. A claim that rests on a file's contents or a line number is re-read there before it goes in the PR body; a worktree or a stale checkout gives line numbers that do not exist for the reviewer.
- **Absence of imports is not absence of use.** `grep <package>` returning nothing means the package is reached some other way, not that it is unused. Runtime patching (`ddtrace` instruments Flask and Celery without an import), default resolution (`certifi` is what `requests` picks up as its CA bundle), entry points, and transitive dependencies all bypass the grep. Find the real consumer before calling anything a leaf.
- **A private API the code reaches into is checked directly, every time.** Underscore-prefixed attributes carry no compatibility promise, so a minor bump is free to change them. Instantiate both versions and assert the behavior the code depends on.
- **Set versions in `pyproject.toml` and regenerate with `uv lock`.** Never hand-resolve the lockfile, and never cherry-pick Dependabot's lockfile commits onto the branch: several bumps touching the same block conflict with each other.
- **One host PR, one commit per package.** The host is an existing Dependabot PR (picked by blast-radius class, ties to the lowest number); every other surviving bump becomes a commit on its branch, so a bad bump is reverted on its own without dragging the rest of the queue with it. Opening a separate PR is the fallback for a rejected push, not the default.
- **A dependency bump is a non-integration PR**, so its body sets ``test override: `yarn test nonints` `` (`.claude/rules/pull-requests.md`). Do not let the full integration suite run: it is slow and hits real vendor APIs.
- **`yarn test` is the only test entry point** (never raw `pytest`), and ad-hoc Python is `uv run python3` (`.claude/rules/code-style.md`). Flags: `.claude/skills/run-scripts/guides/test.md`.
- **A comment beside a pin in `pyproject.toml` is a decision, not a stale note.** Some state a hard bound (`celery==5.5.3` cannot go to 5.6.x, `patchright` needs `<1.57.0`); others say why the pin exists and what to check when it moves (`certifi` for the DM and FedEx chains, `pydantic` because stagehand extract schemas are pydantic models). A bump past a stated bound is dropped from the queue with the comment quoted in the PR body, not bumped and tested. `.github/dependabot.yml` carries the rest of the bounds, including the apiflask major ignore.
- **A major version bump is worked or dropped, never bundled quietly.** It gets its own vetting pass; if the evidence does not come back clean, drop it from the host PR and say in the body that it was left open for a separate look.
- **Failures are reported, not worked around.** A bump whose evidence comes back bad is dropped from the branch and named in the body with what broke. Pinning around it, adding a shim, or weakening a test to accommodate it are all out of scope for this skill.

## Don't

- **Don't** treat a green `yarn test nonints` as the evidence for a silent-runtime, trust-anchor, contract, or infrastructure bump. It is the floor for every bump and the whole story only for leaves.
- **Don't** read only the release notes. They are a starting point for what to look for in the diff, never a substitute for it.
- **Don't** open one PR per bump, and don't leave the superseded ones unnamed — a human has to find them to close them.
- **Don't** leave Dependabot's generated body on the host PR. It is a changelog dump for one package and no longer describes the diff; the evidence body replaces it wholesale.
- **Don't** include a bump whose target version is already on `main`. Dependabot leaves stale PRs open after a combined merge; those are closed, not re-landed.
- **Don't** widen the diff. The branch changes `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, and `package.json` only. A source change needed to accommodate a bump means that bump comes out of the queue and gets its own PR.

style.prompt:
# Concise

Default to brevity. Lead with the answer or result, then only the detail that earns its place. Plain language, short paragraphs, no padding. Full sentences, not telegraphic fragments.

Most turns are one to a few sentences of prose. Match length to the question: a single fact is a single line; a real investigation earns its evidence trail, but nothing earns filler. Reviewing a reply should never feel daunting — if it looks like a document, it's too much for a chat turn.

## Cut

- Preamble and restating the question. Open with the answer.
- Closing summaries, recaps, and "let me know if..." sign-offs.
- Narration of what you are about to do or just did with tools. Let the actions and their results stand. One short heading before a big batch of work is fine; a play-by-play is not.
- Hedging and filler ("I think", "it's worth noting", "basically", "delve", "leverage", "robust", "seamless", "in order to").
- Decorative structure. Headings, tables, and bold section labels are for genuinely structured content (a field-by-field comparison, a set of IDs, a result matrix), not for dressing up an answer that a sentence or two would carry. Prose is the default; reach for structure only when the data is actually a table or the user asked. When in doubt, write the sentence.

## Keep (brevity means cutting filler, not substance)

- The evidence behind a claim: `file:line` references, raw values, exact numbers, error text, timestamps. Specifics are the point, not padding.
- The reasoning that justifies a non-obvious conclusion, and any caveat that changes the reader's decision. When debugging or investigating, show the trail that proves the finding, not just the verdict.
- Enough context that the answer stands on its own.

## Scope: everything you write, not just chat

The same bar applies to every word produced — chat replies, code comments, commit messages, PR bodies, Linear cards, docs, test narration. Start from nothing and add only what the reader needs; if a sentence restates what they can already see (the code, the diff, the error message beside it), delete it. Surface-specific rules stack on top of this, they never loosen it:

- Anything another person reads (customer/vendor messages, Linear, PR titles and descriptions) follows `communications.md` and, unless it is a one-liner, goes through the `claudish-output` skill before it is sent.
- Code comments follow `code-style.md`: none by default, ELI5 when the code alone can't carry the why.

When the user asks for depth, a walkthrough, or a full writeup, give it. Concise is the default, not a ceiling.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- integration-api-validator: Validates an external integration's API before any code is written. Characterizes transport, auth, pagination, response format, token refresh, and webhook style; identifies the closest existing integration as exemplar via parallel Explore searches. Use when starting a new integration via /plan-integration, or ad-hoc to re-characterize an existing integration whose source API has changed (vendor migration, new endpoints, deprecation). Outputs `.claude/references/{name}/api-summary.md`. (Tools: Bash, Read, Write, WebFetch, Grep, Glob)

- integration-data-seeder: Seeds a vendor's writes-safe sandbox with enough test data for downstream function-writer validation — products, inventory, orders distributed across states, returns, inbound shipments — and attempts state transitions (ship, cancel, process). Records under api-summary.md "Sandbox seeding" what was created and any state transitions that couldn't be driven via API (vendor UI required, real carrier needed, etc.). Spawned by the orchestrator after `integration-api-validator` finishes characterization, when the validator's reads turned up a thin or empty sandbox. Single-pass agent — runs once per integration build. (Tools: Bash, Read, Write, WebFetch, Grep, Glob)

- integration-function-writer: Implements one coherent unit of integration code — either a single data function (get_orders, get_inventory, write_order, etc.) or the auth bundle (get_integration_secret + <name>_request + validate_integration_secret). Iterates with yarn crawl + yarn test until validated. Standard path is via /plan-integration after the api-validator has produced api-summary.md. Can also be invoked ad-hoc for a single-method add to an existing integration when the exemplar is already known. Adheres strictly to .claude/references/integration-patterns.md. (Tools: Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- integration-reviewer: Reviews a single unit of integration code (one data function, the auth bundle, or a single test file) against `.claude/references/integration-patterns.md`. Pattern-matches against the exemplar from api-summary.md when present. Runs targeted `yarn test`. Emits a structured BLOCK / APPROVE / APPROVE_WITH_NOTES verdict. Has no edit access — surfaces findings only. Use after each integration-function-writer invocation in /plan-integration, OR ad-hoc to review a single file or diff when debugging an integration, investigating a customer issue, or pre-PR. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. - agent-pylon-investigate: Autonomous Pylon-ticket investigator for an unattended cloud routine. Fired once per new ticket by a Pylon webhook. Triage (skip noise / route non-technical / investigate) → check prior art → wrap the `investigate` skill → post a Pylon INTERNAL NOTE, and open a draft PR for a clear fix to the reported bug. Unrelated bugs found along the way go in the note, not a PR, and become a Linear card only when they would otherwise be lost. Fully unattended, internal-only. Use when handed a Pylon issue id (UUID) in a routine session.
- bulk-resync: Bulk resync connections for a given org and integration. Queries DynamoDB for connection IDs and runs the resync script.
- claudish-output: Rewrite the wording of an external output (PR title or body, Linear card, Slack or email reply, commit message, doc paragraph) into plain English, in the voice of .claude/rules/communications.md, with the claudish-to-english prompts before it leaves the session; Claude Haiku does the rewrite through the session's own Claude Code binary, on a laptop or in a cloud session alike, and the repo display hook's other providers (ollama, anthropic, openai, codex) are a flag away. Use when the user says "claudish to english", "put this through claudish", "claudish the title/body", or asks for an outgoing text's language changed or made plain. Only prose is rewritten; templates, machine-read lines, fenced blocks and links pass through untouched.
- configure-schedule: Adjust crawl schedules for connections by modifying DynamoDB scheduler rows
- create-linear-issue: The one surface that creates a Linear issue. Two modes — compose a card from a freeform human ask (pick the Type label + integration/customer label, write a short human body), or file a caller-supplied spec from an automated skill like stale-schedule-investigate, which keeps the caller's title, labels and fenced blocks but trims its prose to the body ceiling and lands it in Robot Draft. Always reads the live workspace labels and statuses, and never invents a label. Use when asked to file/create/open a Linear issue, ticket, or card, and whenever another skill needs to create one. Out of scope: editing or closing existing issues.
- distill: Weekly consolidation pass over the .claude/ markdown — compact api-summary files to current API behavior, promote patterns humans taught via PR review into gotchas / rules / CLAUDE.md, and fix skill instructions whose output humans corrected on review. Use for the scheduled distillation routine or ad hoc when knowledge files have drifted into append-only history (`/distill [--lookback <days>]`). Markdown only: no code edits; the deliverable is a single draft PR.
- fan-out-change: Make one change ripple correctly across every integration (or every file in a large set) — a new canonical field, a renamed helper, a formatter-shape change, a signature migration. Use when a single schema/infra edit forces a matching edit in dozens or hundreds of `integrations/**/integration.py` files and each site needs per-integration judgment (real value vs IntegrationNotImplemented, docs-first surfacing, FOLLOW-UP when unverifiable) rather than a blind find-replace. Fan out by file/integration, each agent owning a slice; verify structurally before trusting any "done".
- fix-tests: Analyze failing tests from the daily CI report (Slack), a GitHub Actions run, or pasted yarn test output and implement root-cause fixes — both integration tests (live vendor crawls in test/integrations) and non-integration tests (api / celery / lambda / utils / transports). Use when asked to fix failing tests, work the daily CI failure report, or when given pytest failures. Every failure is reproduced and classified before any edit — never a green-at-any-cost shortcut like ignoring validation, weakening an assert, or skipping.
- installation-guide: Create or refresh the customer-facing Notion installation guide for an integration (lives under the Integration Installation Guides page in the trackstarhq workspace) and set `installation_guide_url` in the integration's manifest.json to the public trackstar.notion.site URL — or, for plain-oauth installs, ensure the manifest carries no guide URL at all. Invoked via Skill() by /plan-integration once the scaffold manifest exists, or by a person running `/installation-guide <name>` to backfill a missing or placeholder guide. Only for that one integration's guide: never auto-invoke from prose that merely mentions a guide, Notion, or a manifest, since a run creates a page in the shared trackstarhq workspace and edits manifest.json.
- integration-pr: Create or refresh a pokedex integration PR — body and field-mapping comment. Default behavior is create-from-current-branch; positional PR URL / `#NN` switches to refresh mode (detect-and-patch the existing body + mapping comment). Triggered by `/integration-pr [<pr>]`, or invoked via Skill() by `/wrap-integration` step 8 and `/plan-integration` finalize — the canonical PR-creation surface for orchestrating skills. Only for integration PRs — never invoke for a non-integration branch, and never auto-invoke from prose that merely mentions opening a PR.
- inventory-mapping: Build an inventory field-mapping breakdown — how each canonical Trackstar inventory field (awaiting/onhand/committed/unfulfillable/fulfillable/sellable) is derived from a given WMS integration's source fields. Use when a customer or ticket asks how Trackstar inventory fields map to the underlying integration.
- investigate: Investigate Trackstar integration issues — missing data, field mismatches, webhook failures, sync delays, stale schedules, crawl errors, credential problems, and customer-reported bugs. Use when debugging any connection issue, when a customer reports data problems, when schedules are stale, when analyzing Datadog error logs, or when triaging a support thread. Always use this skill for any Trackstar investigation, even if the issue type isn't immediately clear.
- knowledge-base: Read the Greptile knowledge base — Greptile's synthesized architecture docs for every trackstarhq repo (pokedex, oak, pokecenter, eevvee, documentation, and more) — to get oriented in code before reading it. Use when you need to understand how a subsystem works, when planning or reviewing a change in code you have not read, when onboarding to an unfamiliar area, or when a question spans a sibling repo that is not checked out locally. Also covers the custom-context rules Greptile applies when it reviews a PR, and verifying that Greptile is configured before relying on any of it.
- pylon: Fetch Pylon issues, read messages, and post private (internal) notes via the Pylon REST API. Use when looking up a Pylon ticket by id, reading its message thread, or adding an internal note. Replaces the pylon MCP tools.
- query-datadog: How to query Datadog logs for Trackstar crawler investigations — the tags-vs-attributes distinction, the standard crawler log query for a connection / integration / function, pinning the time window to the staleness range, and building shareable Datadog links for PRs and Linear cards. Use whenever querying Datadog for a stale schedule, crawl error, sync issue, or any connection problem.
- review-code: Review integration code for quality, pattern adherence, and production readiness before merging
- review-dependabot-prs: Vet the open Dependabot bumps in pokedex and fold them into one of the existing Dependabot PRs, whose body becomes the evidence. Use when asked to review, triage, or clear the Dependabot queue, or when dependency-bump PRs have piled up. Each package is classified by blast radius and vetted against the code that actually uses it — a clean import and a green test run are not evidence for anything that fails silently in production. Opens the PR ready for a human; never merges it.
- run-scripts: Canonical invocations for the pokedex yarn scripts (yarn test, yarn crawl, yarn curl, yarn serve, yarn generate, yarn install-integration, yarn worker). Use whenever about to run tests, invoke pytest, exercise an integration method, scaffold a new integration, push dev credentials, or hit the local Pokedex API. **Required reading before running any tests** — never invoke `python -m pytest` or `pytest` directly; always use `yarn test` with the right filters.
- scrape-docs: Scrape and process API documentation from URLs, PDFs, or OpenAPI specs into LLM-optimized markdown
- se-investigate: Solutions-Engineer front door for a Pylon ticket. Triage (skip noise / route non-technical / investigate), check if we've already answered it (Slack + past Pylon tickets), run the investigation, then post findings as a Pylon INTERNAL NOTE. Use when handed a Pylon ticket id to investigate end-to-end. Runs unattended (a local poller opens a session per new ticket - see https://github.com/trackstarhq/pylon-dispatcher).
- stale-schedule-dispatch: Triage stale Trackstar crawl schedules and fan out one investigation per root-cause cluster. Use to run the stale-schedule dispatcher (scheduled routine or ad hoc) — pull the stale set, drop what shouldn't be worked on, dedup against in-flight investigations via the scheduler-row pointer, cluster by root cause, and fire one investigator per cluster. Read-only: no code edits, no PRs, no DynamoDB writes.
- stale-schedule-investigate: Diagnose the root cause of one stale Trackstar crawl-schedule cluster and either ship a tested fix as a PR or escalate with evidence. Use when handed a stale-schedule cluster (the dispatcher's /fire payload, or ad hoc) — investigate root cause, open the Linear issue, write the investigation pointer to the scheduler rows, then act per classification (code fix + PR, or escalate / customer / vendor / infra). Composes the read-only `investigate` skill for diagnosis.
- update-crawl-frequency: Update crawl_frequencies on a connection to change how often specific flows sync
- validate-api: Validate API behavior before implementation by testing auth, collecting samples, and documenting discrepancies
- catchup: Catchup - Review Branch Changes
- debug-report: Debug Report - Investigate Customer Issues
- diagram-trackstar: Regenerate the Trackstar architecture diagrams in docs/architecture/, grounded in real code
- generate-support-email: Generate Support Email - Draft Email to WMS/API Vendor
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Two modes — compose a card from a freeform human ask (pick the Type label + integration/customer label, write a short human body), or file a caller-supplied spec from an automated skill like stale-schedule-investigate, which keeps the caller's title, labels and fenced blocks but trims its prose to the body ceiling and lands it in Robot Draft. Always reads the live workspace labels and statuses, and never invents a label. Use when asked to file/create/open a Linear issue, ticket, or card, and whenever another skill needs to create one. Out of scope: editing or closing existing issues.
- distill: Weekly consolidation pass over the .claude/ markdown — compact api-summary files to current API behavior, promote patterns humans taught via PR review into gotchas / rules / CLAUDE.md, and fix skill instructions whose output humans corrected on review. Use for the scheduled distillation routine or ad hoc when knowledge files have drifted into append-only history (`/distill [--lookback <days>]`). Markdown only: no code edits; the deliverable is a single draft PR.
- fan-out-change: Make one change ripple correctly across every integration (or every file in a large set) — a new canonical field, a renamed helper, a formatter-shape change, a signature migration. Use when a single schema/infra edit forces a matching edit in dozens or hundreds of `integrations/**/integration.py` files and each site needs per-integration judgment (real value vs IntegrationNotImplemented, docs-first surfacing, FOLLOW-UP when unverifiable) rather than a blind find-replace. Fan out by file/integration, each agent owning a slice; verify structurally before trusting any "done".
- fix-tests: Analyze failing tests from the daily CI report (Slack), a GitHub Actions run, or pasted yarn test output and implement root-cause fixes — both integration tests (live vendor crawls in test/integrations) and non-integration tests (api / celery / lambda / utils / transports). Use when asked to fix failing tests, work the daily CI failure report, or when given pytest failures. Every failure is reproduced and classified before any edit — never a green-at-any-cost shortcut like ignoring validation, weakening an assert, or skipping.
- installation-guide: Create or refresh the customer-facing Notion installation guide for an integration (lives under the Integration Installation Guides page in the trackstarhq workspace) and set `installation_guide_url` in the integration's manifest.json to the public trackstar.notion.site URL — or, for plain-oauth installs, ensure the manifest carries no guide URL at all. Invoked via Skill() by /plan-integration once the scaffold manifest exists, or by a person running `/installation-guide <name>` to backfill a missing or placeholder guide. Only for that one integration's guide: never auto-invoke from prose that merely mentions a guide, Notion, or a manifest, since a run creates a page in the shared trackstarhq workspace and edits manifest.json.
- integration-pr: Create or refresh a pokedex integration PR — body and field-mapping comment. Default behavior is create-from-current-branch; positional PR URL / `#NN` switches to refresh mode (detect-and-patch the existing body + mapping comment). Triggered by `/integration-pr [<pr>]`, or invoked via Skill() by `/wrap-integration` step 8 and `/plan-integration` finalize — the canonical PR-creation surface for orchestrating skills. Only for integration PRs — never invoke for a non-integration branch, and never auto-invoke from prose that merely mentions opening a PR.
- inventory-mapping: Build an inventory field-mapping breakdown — how each canonical Trackstar inventory field (awaiting/onhand/committed/unfulfillable/fulfillable/sellable) is derived from a given WMS integration's source fields. Use when a customer or ticket asks how Trackstar inventory fields map to the underlying integration.
- investigate: Investigate Trackstar integration issues — missing data, field mismatches, webhook failures, sync delays, stale schedules, crawl errors, credential problems, and customer-reported bugs. Use when debugging any connection issue, when a customer reports data problems, when schedules are stale, when analyzing Datadog error logs, or when triaging a support thread. Always use this skill for any Trackstar investigation, even if the issue type isn't immediately clear.
- knowledge-base: Read the Greptile knowledge base — Greptile's synthesized architecture docs for every trackstarhq repo (pokedex, oak, pokecenter, eevvee, documentation, and more) — to get oriented in code before reading it. Use when you need to understand how a subsystem works, when planning or reviewing a change in code you have not read, when onboarding to an unfamiliar area, or when a question spans a sibling repo that is not checked out locally. Also covers the custom-context rules Greptile applies when it reviews a PR, and verifying that Greptile is configured before relying on any of it.
- pylon: Fetch Pylon issues, read messages, and post private (internal) notes via the Pylon REST API. Use when looking up a Pylon ticket by id, reading its message thread, or adding an internal note. Replaces the pylon MCP tools.
- query-datadog: How to query Datadog logs for Trackstar crawler investigations — the tags-vs-attributes distinction, the standard crawler log query for a connection / integration / function, pinning the time window to the staleness range, and building shareable Datadog links for PRs and Linear cards. Use whenever querying Datadog for a stale schedule, crawl error, sync issue, or any connection problem.
- review-code: Review integration code for quality, pattern adherence, and production readiness before merging
- review-dependabot-prs: Vet the open Dependabot bumps in pokedex and fold them into one of the existing Dependabot PRs, whose body becomes the evidence. Use when asked to review, triage, or clear the Dependabot queue, or when dependency-bump PRs have piled up. Each package is classified by blast radius and vetted against the code that actually uses it — a clean import and a green test run are not evidence for anything that fails silently in production. Opens the PR ready for a human; never merges it.
- run-scripts: Canonical invocations for the pokedex yarn scripts (yarn test, yarn crawl, yarn curl, yarn serve, yarn generate, yarn install-integration, yarn worker). Use whenever about to run tests, invoke pytest, exercise an integration method, scaffold a new integration, push dev credentials, or hit the local Pokedex API. **Required reading before running any tests** — never invoke `python -m pytest` or `pytest` directly; always use `yarn test` with the right filters.
- scrape-docs: Scrape and process API documentation from URLs, PDFs, or OpenAPI specs into LLM-optimized markdown
- se-investigate: Solutions-Engineer front door for a Pylon ticket. Triage (skip noise / route non-technical / investigate), check if we've already answered it (Slack + past Pylon tickets), run the investigation, then post findings as a Pylon INTERNAL NOTE. Use when handed a Pylon ticket id to investigate end-to-end. Runs unattended (a local poller opens a session per new ticket - see https://github.com/trackstarhq/pylon-dispatcher).
- stale-schedule-dispatch: Triage stale Trackstar crawl schedules and fan out one investigation per root-cause cluster. Use to run the stale-schedule dispatcher (scheduled routine or ad hoc) — pull the stale set, drop what shouldn't be worked on, dedup against in-flight investigations via the scheduler-row pointer, cluster by root cause, and fire one investigator per cluster. Read-only: no code edits, no PRs, no DynamoDB writes.
- stale-schedule-investigate: Diagnose the root cause of one stale Trackstar crawl-schedule cluster and either ship a tested fix as a PR or escalate with evidence. Use when handed a stale-schedule cluster (the dispatcher's /fire payload, or ad hoc) — investigate root cause, open the Linear issue, write the investigation pointer to the scheduler rows, then act per classification (code fix + PR, or escalate / customer / vendor / infra). Composes the read-only `investigate` skill for diagnosis.
- update-crawl-frequency: Update crawl_frequencies on a connection to change how often specific flows sync
- validate-api: Validate API behavior before implementation by testing auth, collecting samples, and documenting discrepancies
- catchup: Catchup - Review Branch Changes
- debug-report: Debug Report - Investigate Customer Issues
- diagram-trackstar: Regenerate the Trackstar architecture diagrams in docs/architecture/, grounded in real code
- generate-support-email: Generate Support Email - Draft Email to WMS/API Vendor
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
- anthropic-skills:docs: docs (living docs people share, comment on and edit; use only when the user asks for one: names a doc, document, page, memo, spec, PRD, runbook or write-up, asks for somewhere to share or keep editing something, or says yes to your doc offer; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat (at most a one-line doc offer); a report, status update, recap or "something I can send them" with no form named → ask first: reply, doc or file?; tabs hold tables and live charts too; a pasted claude.ai/code/artifact/… link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; not HTML pages, apps or plain chat answers; a .docx/.pptx/.xlsx/PDF asked for by name → that format's skill): asked for one → no docs-connector instructions in context? call the docs connector's `guide` with topic.instructions first, then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached. Documenting code means docstrings or repo docs, not a doc.
- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.
- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
</system-reminder>

# Trackstar - Integration Platform

## Project Overview

Trackstar unifies e-commerce and logistics integrations into normalized APIs.

**Components:**

- **pokedex** (Python/Flask) - Core API backend (port 8000)
- **eevvee** (React) - Auth modal (port 3005)
- **pokecenter** (React) - Admin dashboard (port 3000)

## Quick Start

```bash

yarn serve        # flask API
yarn worker       # celery worker
yarn test         # run tests
yarn crawl        # test integration method
yarn generate     # scaffold new integration
```

## Project Structure

```txt
trackstar/
├── pokedex/          # backend (Flask, Celery)
│   ├── integrations/ # integration code (wms/, cart/, freight/)
│   ├── resources/    # marshmallow schemas
│   └── test/         # test suites
├── eevvee/           # auth modal (React)
├── pokecenter/       # admin UI (React)
└── .claude/
    ├── knowledge/    # integration examples index
    ├── skills/       # reusable workflows
    ├── commands/     # slash commands
    ├── schemas/      # resource field definitions
    └── plans/        # implementation plans (gitignored)
```

## Code Style

- no docstrings - code is self-documenting
- minimal comments (lowercase, 5-10 words, explain why not what)
- favor simplicity over cleverness
- error-driven development - let errors guide fixes, try not to use .get
- avoid list comprehensions and code like formatted_inventory.append(format(item)) - separate into multiple lines for readability and easier debugging (e.g formatted_item = format(item); formatted_inventory.append(formatted_item))
- for pokedex - if "created_date" and "updated_date" are not implemented, don't add it in the integration formatter code. don't add trackstar_tags either

## Integration Development

1. Read `.claude/knowledge/integration-examples.md` to find similar integrations
2. Study the actual implementation code (always up to date)
3. Use `/plan-integration` for complex work
4. Test incrementally with `yarn crawl`

**IntegrationNotImplemented vs None:**
- `IntegrationNotImplemented` means the field is not available at all from the integration — no endpoint or data source provides it
- If even one code path provides a field, all other paths must set it to `None`, not `IntegrationNotImplemented`
- There will never be a case where we see code like `x = y or IntegrationNotImplemented` or `x = data.get(y, IntegrationNotImplemented)`

## Testing

After making changes, run targeted tests. See `run-scripts` skill for filter options.

**Exemplar integrations:**
- WMS: deposco, shipbob, ongoing
- Cart: shopify, etsy, amazon

## Available Commands

- `/catchup` - review branch changes
- `/plan-integration` - start integration planning
- `/pr` - prepare pull request
- `/debug-report` - investigate customer issues
- `/generate-support-email` - draft email to WMS/API vendor

## Available Skills

- **scrape-docs** - scrape API documentation into LLM-optimized markdown
- **validate-api** - test API auth and collect samples before implementation
- **run-scripts** - reference for crawl, test, curl, serve, generate commands
- **review-code** - code review checklist for production readiness
- **issue-debugging** - investigating trackstar issues (missing data, webhooks, sync, stale schedules, errors)
- **worktree** - manage git worktrees for feature branches (`/worktree add|remove branch-name`)

## Context Management

- clear context at 60k tokens (use /clear)
- for complex tasks: document progress to .md, clear, continue
- read knowledge files on-demand, don't preload
- use Planning Mode for complex integration work

## Working Directories

- plans go in `pokedex/../.claude/plans/` (gitignored)
- temp scripts go in `pokedex/../.claude/tmp/` (gitignored)
- scraped docs go in `pokedex/../.claude/references/{integration}/` (gitignored)

# Trackstar - Integration Platform

## Project Overview

Trackstar unifies e-commerce and logistics integrations into normalized APIs.

**Components:**

- **pokedex** (Python/Flask) — Core API backend (port 8000). This file is the entry point.
- **eevvee** (React) — Customer-facing auth modal (port 3005). [trackstarhq/eevvee](https://github.com/trackstarhq/eevvee) · [`CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/trackstarhq/eevvee/blob/main/CLAUDE.md)
- **pokecenter** (React) — Customer admin dashboard (port 3000). [trackstarhq/pokecenter](https://github.com/trackstarhq/pokecenter) · [`CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/trackstarhq/pokecenter/blob/main/CLAUDE.md)
- **oak** (Next.js) — Internal observability + admin (port 3000; runs separately from pokecenter). [trackstarhq/oak](https://github.com/trackstarhq/oak) · [`CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/trackstarhq/oak/blob/main/CLAUDE.md)
- **documentation** (Mintlify) — Public docs site at docs.trackstarhq.com. [trackstarhq/documentation](https://github.com/trackstarhq/documentation) · [`CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/trackstarhq/documentation/blob/main/CLAUDE.md)

The sibling CLAUDE.md files cover stack-specific conventions, page-by-page entry points, and deploy details for each component. Read the one for the repo you're working in.

## Quick Start

```bash

yarn serve        # flask API
yarn worker       # celery worker
yarn test         # run tests
yarn crawl        # test integration method
yarn generate     # scaffold new integration
```

## Project Structure

```txt
trackstar/
├── pokedex/              # backend (Flask, Celery)
│   ├── integrations/     # integration code (wms/, cart/, carrier/, freight/)
│   ├── resources/        # canonical schemas (no vendor names — see Code Style)
│   ├── test/             # test suites
│   └── .claude/          # skills, knowledge, references — committed, not a submodule
│       ├── knowledge/    # integration examples and gotchas
│       ├── skills/       # reusable workflows (incl. /plan-integration, /investigate)
│       ├── commands/     # slash commands (catchup, debug-report, generate-support-email)
│       ├── agents/       # subagents (see "Available Subagents")
│       ├── references/   # operational rules + per-integration api-summary
│       └── plans/        # implementation plans (gitignored)
├── eevvee/               # auth modal (React)
├── pokecenter/           # admin UI (React)
├── oak/                  # internal observability + admin (Next.js)
└── documentation/        # Mintlify docs site
```

## Where to look

| Need | Path |
|---|---|
| Operational rules for integration code | `.claude/references/integration-patterns.md` |
| Pattern-indexed exemplars (auth, pagination, enrichment) | `.claude/knowledge/integration-examples.md` |
| Known integration quirks / gotchas | `.claude/knowledge/integration-gotchas.md` |
| Yarn script flags (test, crawl, curl, install) | `.claude/skills/run-scripts/` |
| Per-integration API characterization | `.claude/references/{name}/api-summary.md` |
| Subagents (reviewer, function-writer, api-validator) | `.claude/agents/` |
| Integration code | `pokedex/integrations/{wms,cart,carrier}/{name}/` |
| Canonical schemas (the only source of truth — never duplicated anywhere) | `pokedex/resources/{type}/*.py` |
| What Greptile reads on a PR (points at the rules above, doesn't copy them) | `.greptile/files.json` |
| How a subsystem works, across any trackstarhq repo (Greptile knowledge base) | `.claude/skills/knowledge-base/` |
| How a Linear card should read, and when to file one at all | `.claude/rules/communications.md` "Linear cards" |

## Code Style

Always-on subset: [`.claude/rules/code-style.md`](.claude/rules/code-style.md) — no docstrings outside the published-text exceptions listed there; no comment unless the change isn't obvious from the code (default is none, delete when in doubt), and keepers are lowercase, ELI5-plain, why-not-what (one-read test: any SWE understands it in one pass, no jargon, noun-stacks, or arrow-chains); no leading-underscore "private" names; reuse the codebase's verbs, never coin one (grep before naming; status strings match the error text); error-driven (avoid `.get`); no comprehensions in integration code; `logger`/`print` discipline; constants in `config.py` (`import config`, don't scatter `os.environ.get`). Full reviewer checklist: [`.claude/references/integration-patterns.md`](.claude/references/integration-patterns.md) "Code style". Field-output invariants (dates, `trackstar_tags`, `IntegrationNotImplemented` vs `None`): [`.claude/rules/integration-fidelity.md`](.claude/rules/integration-fidelity.md). Canonical schemas (`resources/<type>/*.py`) never name vendors — keep "NetSuite", "Shopify", etc. inside `integrations/`.

## Git Workflow

[`.claude/rules/git-workflow.md`](.claude/rules/git-workflow.md): never commit to `main`; create the branch before any code change (a prerequisite, not a post-step); `cd` to the worktree first if one is specified; branch naming `{feature-or-fix-description}`.

## Integration Development

**Freight integrations are out of scope.** Decline if asked to build one; existing freight code is maintained but not extended.

1. Find a similar integration in [`.claude/knowledge/integration-examples.md`](.claude/knowledge/integration-examples.md) — exemplars are picked by API shape (transport, auth, pagination), not type.
2. Study the actual implementation code (always up to date).
3. `/plan-integration` builds a NEW integration autonomously; `/iterate-integration` adds a function or fixes one.
4. Test incrementally with `yarn crawl`.

The doctrine an integration must follow lives in three always-on rules plus one full checklist — **read the checklist before any non-trivial integration edit:**

- [`.claude/rules/integration-fidelity.md`](.claude/rules/integration-fidelity.md) — faithfully represent the source API: loud failures > quiet workarounds, spec-is-canonical, root-cause-first before any escape hatch, the shallow-fix family, `IntegrationNotImplemented` vs `None`, date / `trackstar_tags` invariants.
- [`.claude/rules/write-safety.md`](.claude/rules/write-safety.md) — `allow_writes()` / `test_account()`, never write to vendor prod (HTTP method isn't the gate; the operation's effect on vendor data is).
- [`.claude/rules/integration-testing.md`](.claude/rules/integration-testing.md) — the live `TestX` class is the only test surface; never modify a failing test to pass.
- [`.claude/references/integration-patterns.md`](.claude/references/integration-patterns.md) — the full pass/fail checklist subagents enforce (format output shape, data access, file structure + ordering, resource scope + dependency chains, write safety, code style). The source of truth, covering cases the rules summarize.

## Testing

`yarn test` with filters is the only test entry point — **never** `python -m pytest` / raw `pytest`; for ad-hoc Python use `uv run python3`, never raw `python3` (both in [`.claude/rules/code-style.md`](.claude/rules/code-style.md); flags in the `run-scripts` skill). Integration test rules: [`.claude/rules/integration-testing.md`](.claude/rules/integration-testing.md).

## Available Commands

- `/catchup` - review branch changes
- `/debug-report` - investigate customer issues
- `/generate-support-email` - draft email to WMS/API vendor
- `/claudish` - opt in to (or pause, restyle, or inspect) the plain-language rewrite of assistant messages on your own screen; off for everyone until `/claudish on` (see `.claude/hooks/README.md`)

## Available Skills

- **plan-integration** - autonomously build a NEW integration end-to-end: no human gates, parallel resource-cluster fan-out in worktrees, park-and-continue on non-convergence, PR opened ready for review + Slack/Linear status; humans review via PR comments (`/plan-integration <ticket-url-or-paste>`, or put the `bot-build` label on a Linear issue)
- **iterate-integration** - run the writer+reviewer loop on existing integration code for fix-type work (failing tests, customer-issue fixes, regression patches) (`/iterate-integration "<task>" [--ship]`)

Never merges (`/review-dependabot-prs`)
- **integration-pr** - create or refresh a pokedex integration PR (body + field-mapping comment). No arg = create from current branch; positional `<pr>` = refresh existing PR via detect-and-patch (`/integration-pr [<pr-url-or-number>]`)

Its mechanics are reused by reference inside `/plan-integration` (compose + finalize); run it standalone on a hand-built integration (`/wrap-integration`)
- **installation-guide** - create the customer-facing Notion installation guide (Installation Guides page, trackstarhq workspace) and set `installation_guide_url` in the manifest; the manifest test asserts the guide is publicly readable and non-empty. Invoked during scaffolding, or standalone to backfill placeholder guides (`/installation-guide <integration-name>`)
- **knowledge-base** - read Greptile's synthesized architecture docs for any trackstarhq repo (including siblings not checked out here) to get oriented before reading code, and see the custom-context rules Greptile reviews PRs against; verifies Greptile is configured first
