new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

# Phase 1 — Vet: the per-package evidence loop

Goal: one verdict line per surviving row, each backed by evidence a reviewer can re-run. Run the loop once per package. Nothing is committed in this phase.

## Step 1 — Find the real consumer

Grep first, but do not stop at a miss:

```bash
git fetch origin main
grep -rnE "^\s*(import|from) <module>" --include=*.py . | grep -vE "^\./(\.venv|node_modules)"
```

`--include=*.py` and the `.venv` exclusion both matter: without them the installed copy of the package and every other library that depends on it drown the first-party call sites.

**Zero hits does not mean unused.** Check these before concluding anything:

- **Import-time patching.** `ddtrace` instruments Flask, Celery, `requests` and `boto3` with nothing of ours importing it.

```bash
uv pip install --target /tmp/dep-old --no-deps --quiet <package>==<old-version>
uv pip install --target /tmp/dep-new --no-deps --quiet <package>==<new-version>
diff -rq /tmp/dep-old /tmp/dep-new
```


- **The diff is only the version string.** Then the bump changes nothing that runs, and that is the whole finding. State it as what you saw: "diffing the two wheels shows the entire change is the `__version__` string".
- **Code changed, but nothing the call sites touch.** Compare the declared names in each changed module rather than eyeballing the diff:

  ```bash
  done
  ```

```bash

```

```bash

```



# Package playbooks

One section per dependency in `pyproject.toml` and `package.json` that has real blast radius: where it is consumed, what a bump can break, and what proves it did not. Everything else is listed under [Leaves](#leaves).

Line numbers move. Re-read each named file at a fresh `origin/main` before quoting a line in the PR body.

---

## Silent-runtime

### ddtrace

**Consumed by** `utils/logutil.py` (`from ddtrace.trace import tracer as raw_tracer`), and by every Flask request, Celery task, `requests` call and `boto3` call through import-time instrumentation that nothing here imports.

**What can break.** `SafeTracer.local_span_chain` walks `cur._parent`, a private attribute with no compatibility promise, to tag every span up to the service boundary. If `_parent` starts returning `None`, tags land on `current_span()` only and traces silently fragment across `before_request` and `api.*` spans. Nothing raises. There is a comment at the walk saying to re-verify on a bump.

**Prove it.** Install both versions and assert the three properties the walk depends on: `child._parent is parent`, that it returns a `Span` rather than a context object, and that the walk stops when `parent.service != cur.service`. Then run the guards in `test/utils/logutil_test.py` (`test_span_parent_returns_the_parent_span`, `test_local_span_chain_returns_current_then_same_service_parents`, `test_local_span_chain_stops_at_a_different_service`).

For each behavioral change the release claims, resolve its precondition here rather than reporting the claim:

- LLM Observability changes need LLMObs enabled. Check for `DD_LLMOBS_*` in `config.py` and the CDK templates, and for any reference in the codebase.
- Client-IP or request-tag changes affect span tags, not rate limiting: the limiter key comes from Flask's `remote_addr` via `get_remote_address()` at `api.py:379`, fed into `Limiter(key_func=get_rate_limit_key, ...)` at `api.py:400`.

### datadog

**Consumed by** `utils/ecs_protection.py` (`from datadog.dogstatsd.base import statsd` at line 10, `statsd.increment` at line 104).

**What can break.** That metric is the error signal for ECS scale-in protection. A statsd client that silently resolves to a different host or port sends the metric nowhere and the protection stops being observable, with no exception raised.

**Prove it.** Diff `DogStatsd.__init__` between the two versions and follow how host and port resolve when no env var is set. Instantiate both and confirm they land on the same destination, and that `increment` keeps its signature. Then check whether any of the env vars the new version reads (`DD_DOGSTATSD_URL`, `DD_DOGSTATSD_HOST`, and friends) are set anywhere in `config.py` or the CDK templates. `DD_DOGSTATSD_NON_LOCAL_TRAFFIC` in `templates/cluster_services.py` configures the sidecar agent, not this client.

Run `test/celery/ecs_protection_test.py`.

### datadog-lambda

**Consumed by** the Lambda runtime wiring, not by any import of ours: `templates/lambda_services.py:125` sets the container entrypoint to `python -m awslambdaric` with cmd `datadog_lambda.handler.handler`, and `DD_LAMBDA_HANDLER` names the real handler underneath.

**What can break.** If `datadog_lambda.handler.handler` is renamed or moved, every Lambda fails to start at deploy, not at merge. If its wrapper changes what it does to the event or context, handlers see a different payload with nothing local to catch it.

**Prove it.** Confirm `datadog_lambda/handler.py` still exports `handler` in the new version, and diff the wrapper for changes to how it passes the event and context through. Run `yarn test lambda`.

---

## Trust-anchor

### certifi

**Consumed by** nothing directly. It is the default CA bundle `requests` and `httpx` load, and `requests` reaches the image transitively through `curlify` and `datadog`. The pin comment in `pyproject.toml` says it exists for the DM and FedEx certificates.

**What can break.** A retired CA root breaks every TLS handshake to a vendor whose chain terminates there. It fails at crawl time against one vendor, not in CI.

**Prove it.** Diff the bundle by subject and give the root count on each side (the trust-anchor section of [workflows/vet.md](../workflows/vet.md) has the `openssl` pipeline). For every removed root, decide whether it is routine retirement (the same authority's newer roots survive) or a distrust that strands someone. Then resolve the hosts the pin exists for by fetching their live chains and confirming the root each terminates at is present in the new bundle:

```bash
openssl s_client -connect api.distributionmgmt.com:443 -servername api.distributionmgmt.com -showcerts </dev/null 2>/dev/null | grep -E "^ *[0-9] [si]:"
openssl s_client -connect api.fedex.com:443 -servername api.fedex.com -showcerts </dev/null 2>/dev/null | grep -E "^ *[0-9] [si]:"
```

A bump that only adds roots still gets the count reported; a removal is never waved through on the count alone.

### pycryptodome

**Consumed by** `utils/boto.py` (`from Crypto.Cipher import AES` at line 69, `decrypt_and_verify` at line 3020).

**What can break.** That is the path that decrypts stored connection credentials. A changed AES mode default, tag length, or nonce handling makes previously encrypted secrets undecryptable, which surfaces as every connection failing auth rather than as an exception at import.

**Prove it.** Confirm the cipher construction the code uses keeps its signature, then round-trip: encrypt under the old version and decrypt under the new one with the same key and nonce. A ciphertext written by the old version must still open under the new one. Run `test/utils/boto_test.py`.

### cryptography

**Consumed by** `integrations/erp/netsuite/integration.py` (certificate generation, around the `public_bytes(serialization.Encoding.PEM)` call) and, transitively, by `paramiko` for SSH and by `pyjwt` for RS256.

**What can break.** A removed or deprecated primitive breaks NetSuite's certificate flow, SFTP key exchange, or RS256 verification. Majors here remove primitives on a deprecation schedule.

**Prove it.** Check the release for removals, not additions, and match each against the primitives named above. Confirm the NetSuite serialization call still exists with the same signature, and that `pyjwt` and `paramiko` in the lockfile still declare a compatible range.

---

## Contract

### svix

**Consumed by** `utils/svix_util.py`, which imports `ApplicationIn`, `AppPortalAccessIn`, `EventTypeImportOpenApiIn`, `MessageCreateOptions`, `MessageIn` and `Svix` from `svix.api`, plus `HttpError` and `HTTPValidationError` from `svix.exceptions`. Called from `api.py:700` (`create_application`) and `scripts/rollout.py:381` (`import_openapi`). This is the outbound delivery client: signature verification happens on the customer's side, not here.

**What can break.** `message.create` reads `options.with_content`, so `MessageCreateOptions` has to keep that attribute or webhook payloads go out without their bodies. A renamed or removed model class breaks delivery for every customer at once.

**Prove it.** Diff the two wheels. If the whole change is the `__version__` string, that is the finding and there is nothing further to check. Otherwise, confirm each imported name above still exists with the same shape, and run the guard `test_send_message_passes_options_supported_by_installed_svix_sdk` in `test/lambda/webhook_test.py`, plus `test/lambda/submitter_test.py`.

A major bump gets its own pass: check the migration notes for renames across the whole imported set before deciding whether it joins the host PR.

### apiflask and apispec-oneofschema

**Consumed by** `api.py` and `utils/schema.py` (apiflask), `api.py`, `utils/api.py` and `utils/integrations.py` (apispec-oneofschema).

**What can break.** These generate the public OpenAPI spec and validate incoming request bodies. Drift changes the customer-facing API contract and the spec published to the docs site and to Svix event types, without any local call changing.

**Prove it.** Run the openapi test (`yarn test --openapi`) and diff the generated spec against the one on `origin/main`; a spec change is a customer-facing change and belongs in the body whether or not it is intended. `.github/dependabot.yml` ignores apiflask majors because 3.x breaks spec generation (TRA-1989), so a major here should not appear at all.

### stagehand, browserbase and patchright

**Consumed by** `transports/browser/backend.py` (`from stagehand import Stagehand, browserbase`) and `transports/browser/page.py`. `Stagehand` is constructed only in `BrowserbaseBackend`; `LocalBackend` sets `supports_stagehand = False`, so every stagehand call goes through the hosted API.

**What can break.** The param shapes each call site passes. Three matter:

- `act` — `page.py:306` and `page.py:340`, reaching `backend.py:513`, passing `input` plus `options` keys.
- `stagehand_navigate` — `page.py:111`, reaching `backend.py:521`, passing `url`, `wait_until` and `timeout`.
- `extract` — `page.py:70`, reaching `backend.py:516`, passing `instruction` and `schema` (a pydantic model, which is why `pydantic` is pinned).

**Prove it.** Diff the changed param modules and compare declared names on both sides: nothing removed or renamed among the keys the call sites pass. Report per call site with file and line. A bundled binary that changed is a non-finding once you name why it is unreachable (`supports_stagehand` is false on the local backend and every call goes to the hosted API). `patchright` is pinned `<1.57.0` for the local browser, so its bumps are dropped, not vetted.

Run `test/transports/browser_test.py`.

### boto3

**Consumed by** `utils/boto.py` and a handful of integrations. Dependabot ignores its patch releases, so only minors and majors arrive.

**What can break.** DynamoDB, S3 and Secrets Manager calls, plus the serialization boto applies to DynamoDB types. A changed default (retry mode, checksum behavior, endpoint resolution) changes what reaches AWS with no local signature change.

**Prove it.** Read the changelog for default changes rather than new services, and check each against the calls in `utils/boto.py`. Run `yarn test utils` and `yarn test lambda`.

### paramiko

**Consumed by** `transports/sftp_client.py` and `test/integrations/base_test.py`.

**What can break.** Host-key and key-exchange algorithm negotiation. Dropping a legacy algorithm breaks connections to older vendor SFTP servers at crawl time, and nothing in CI touches those servers.

**Prove it.** Read the release for algorithms disabled or removed by default, not for features added. If any were dropped, name the SFTP-based integrations and say the risk is unverified in CI rather than implying it was covered.

### serverless-wsgi

**Consumed by** `lambda_handlers/api.py`.

**Consumed by** `utils/sql.py`.

**Consumed by** `utils/boto.py` (`jwt.encode`/`jwt.decode` for org secrets, and RS256 verification of the Clerk header), `lambda_handlers/billing_export.py`, and the NetSuite and ShipBob integrations.

**Consumed by** `celery_tasks/` and `scripts/crawl.py`. Pinned `5.5.3` with a comment: 5.6.3 fails with `ImportError: The curl client requires the pycurl library`.

**Consumed by** `api.py:400`, where `Limiter` takes `storage_uri=LIMITER_URI` (`config.py:457`, `REDIS_URI` outside local). `redis` itself has no first-party import.

**Consumed by** `api.py`, `utils/middleware.py` and `utils/api.py`.

**Consumed by** `utils/utils.py` (`from pycountry import countries, subdivisions`).

 import itertools

+import os
 import sys

 import typing as t
@@ -27,6 +28,19 @@

+    try:
+        real_exe = os.readlink("/proc/self/exe") if sys.platform == "linux" else ""
+    except OSError:
+        real_exe = ""
+
+    exe = real_exe or (getattr(sys, "executable", "") or "")
+    if not exe:

+
+    return "python" not in os.path.basename(exe).lower()

import sys
from scripts.run import run
from scripts.deploy import build_args_to_stacks, expand_aliases

help_text = """
Usage:  `yarn synth [-s dev|prod] [-h|--help]`
A wrapper around `cdk synth` that takes a stage variable.
Options:
    -s, --stage  Set the stage (default: dev)
    -h, --help   Show this help text
"""


def main():
    synth = "cdk synth"
    stage = "dev"
    help = False
    stacks = []
    args = sys.argv[1:]
    len_args = len(args)
    i = 0
    while i < len_args:
        arg = args[i]
        if arg in ["-h", "--help"]:
            help = True
            synth += " --help"
        elif arg in ["-s", "--stage"]:
            stage = args[i + 1]
            i += 1
        elif not arg.startswith("-"):
            stacks.append(arg)
        else:
            synth += " " + arg
        i += 1

    if not stacks:
        synth += " --all"

    _, args_to_stacks = build_args_to_stacks(stage)
    stacks = expand_aliases(stacks)
    for stack in stacks:
        if stack not in args_to_stacks:
            print(f"Unknown stack: {stack}")
            sys.exit(1)
        synth += f" {args_to_stacks[stack]}"

    if help:
        print(help_text)

    run(synth, stage, False, False, True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Phase 2 — Combine and ship

Goal: every bump that vetted clean folded onto **one of the existing Dependabot PRs**, whose body becomes the evidence. No new branch, no new PR.

## Pick the host PR

The host is the Dependabot PR whose branch carries the whole set. Choose it from the surviving rows:

1. **Highest blast-radius class wins**, in this order: silent-runtime, trust-anchor, contract, infrastructure, leaf. The riskiest package is the one whose name leads the title and whose evidence a reviewer reads first.
2. **Ties break to the lowest PR number.**

If the host's own bump is later dropped, pick the next row by the same rule and start over from its branch. Every other surviving row is a **superseded** PR: named in the body, closed by a human once the host merges.

When only one bump survives the inventory, there is nothing to consolidate. That PR is the host, it gains the evidence body, and nothing is superseded.

## Build on the host's branch

Take the branch name from the host PR's own `head.ref` rather than constructing it. The two ecosystems name their branches differently (`dependabot/uv/{package}-{version}` versus `dependabot/npm_and_yarn/{package}-tw-{version}`), so a constructed name fetches a ref that does not exist:

```bash
HOST_BRANCH=$(<read head.ref from the host PR>)
git fetch origin main "$HOST_BRANCH"
git checkout -B deps-host "origin/$HOST_BRANCH"
git merge origin/main
```

The Dependabot branch already carries its own bump as a commit; the merge brings it up to date with `main`. **Never rebase, amend, or force-push it** — a force-push fights Dependabot for the ref and invalidates anyone's checkout. Only add commits.

Then, **one package at a time**, for every surviving bump except the host's own:

1. Edit the version in `pyproject.toml` (or the range in `package.json`). Leave the comment beside the pin exactly as it is.
2. For a uv bump, regenerate the lockfile: `uv lock`. An npm bump has no committed lockfile, so `package.json` is the whole edit.
3. Commit the pair: `build(deps): bump <package> from <old> to <new>`.

One commit per package is what makes a bad bump revertible without dragging the rest of the queue with it.

**Do not cherry-pick the other Dependabot commits.** Each carries its own resolution of the same `requires-dist` block in `uv.lock`, so they conflict with each other; regenerating from `pyproject.toml` produces one coherent resolution instead. **Do not hand-edit `uv.lock`** for the same reason.

Read the final `uv.lock` diff before touching the PR, when any uv bump is in the set. It should move the bumped packages and their transitives and nothing else. A package moving that no bump named is a finding for the body, not something to leave for the reviewer to spot.

## Verify

```bash
yarn test nonints
```

That is the floor for the whole branch, not the evidence for any individual bump. Name the pass count and call out anything red.

A failure that reproduces identically on `origin/main` is environmental and does not belong to the branch: say which test, say it fails the same way on main, and move on. A failure that is green on main and red here belongs to a bump; find which one, drop it, and say so.

If any bump was Infrastructure-class, the synth diff from Phase 1 runs against this branch's regenerated lockfile, not against a per-package trial.

## Push to the host branch

```bash
git push origin "HEAD:$HOST_BRANCH"
```

No `-u`, no `--force`. Retry a network failure up to four times with exponential backoff (2s, 4s, 8s, 16s).

Once someone other than Dependabot pushes to one of its branches, Dependabot stops rebasing and resolving conflicts on that PR (its own body says so: it maintains the branch "as long as you don't alter it yourself"). That is the intended trade: the branch is yours from this point, so a later conflict with `main` is yours to resolve by merging `main` in again.

**If the push is rejected** (branch protection, or the token has no write access to `dependabot/*`), do not force it. Fall back to a fresh branch from `origin/main` carrying the same commits, open a new PR with the same body, and list every Dependabot PR as superseded including the one that would have been the host. Say in the body that consolidation went to a new branch because the push to the Dependabot branch was rejected.

## Update the host PR

The PR is already open and non-draft, which is where it should stay: the combined PR wants an automated pass and a human review on the evidence.

- **Retitle** it to name every folded package: `build(deps): bump <a>, <b>, <c>`, host first, then the rest in inventory order.
- **Replace the body wholesale.** Dependabot's generated body is a changelog dump for one package and does not describe what is now in the diff. The evidence body replaces it.

Take the replacement body from `.github/pull_request_template.md` and fill it in. **Copy the ship-on-merge block between the `<!-- ship-on-merge -->` markers verbatim and leave every box unticked** — merging is a person's decision and ticking a box makes it a deploy (`.claude/rules/pull-requests.md`).

Set the CI scope by replacing the template's override line with:

    test override: `yarn test nonints`

A dependency bump is a non-integration PR. Do not add a `<!-- auto-tests -->` marker, and do not leave the default `-s`: CI's auto-detect falls back to the full integration suite the moment a non-integration file appears in the diff, which is slow and hits real vendor APIs.

### Body shape

Follow `.claude/rules/communications.md`: lead line, one short paragraph of context, a tight what-changed list, verification. Then the per-package evidence, which is the part that earns its length — it is what the reviewer cannot reconstruct.

1. **Lead line.** What this PR is now: the open Dependabot bumps folded into this one so `uv.lock` resolves once and a human approves once.
2. **Why combined.** One sentence on the shared `requires-dist` block, and that versions were set in `pyproject.toml` and the lockfile regenerated with `uv lock` rather than hand-resolved.
3. **The template checklist**, ticked honestly. "No new tests; existing guards cover the risky bumps" is the accurate note when that is what happened.
4. **What changed** — one line per package, `name old -> new`.
5. **Supersedes.** `Supersedes #A, #B and #C, which can be closed once this merges.` Separately list any PR that is already on `main` and can be closed without merging, and any bump dropped from the queue with its reason (blocked by a pin, major left for its own pass, evidence came back bad).
6. **Per-package evidence**, one bolded paragraph per non-leaf package, ordered by risk with the riskiest first. Each names the call site by file and line, what was checked, and what came back. Leaf packages get a sentence, not a paragraph.
7. **Verification.** The `yarn test nonints` pass count, any named guard tests that ran, and any check that was skipped with the reason it was moot.
8. **The test override line and the ship block.**

Keep the tone plain and specific: no em-dashes, no "this PR elegantly", no reference to the authoring agent.

## Stop here

The skill's end state is the host PR updated and ready for a human. Do not merge it, do not approve it, and do not close the superseded PRs — naming them in the body is the whole handoff.

Report back with the host PR link, the packages folded in, the superseded PR numbers, and the ones dropped with their reasons.

Every uv bump rewrites the same block of `uv.lock`, so landing them one at a time turns the second one into a conflict. Versions were set in `pyproject.toml` and the lockfile regenerated with `uv lock`; nothing in the lockfile was hand-edited. One commit per package, so a bad bump can be reverted on its own.

Checklist before merging:
- [ ] Tests added/updated (no new tests; the existing logutil guards cover the risky one)
- [x] All tests passing
- [ ] [Documentation added/updated](https://github.com/trackstarhq/documentation)
- [ ] [Crawl Best Practices](https://www.notion.so/trackstar/Resource-Crawling-Flow-00a72ce8f2314d4caeec623276daa01b)

## What changed

- ddtrace 4.14.0 -> 4.14.1
- urllib3 2.7.0 -> 2.8.0
- awslambdaric 4.0.3 -> 4.0.4
- datadog-cdk-constructs-v2 5.1.0 -> 5.2.0

`uv.lock` also moves jsii 1.139.0 -> 1.140.0, which datadog-cdk-constructs-v2 5.2.0 requires. Nothing else moved.

Supersedes #6124, #6125 and #6126, which can be closed once this merges. Nothing was dropped from the queue: no bump was already on main, none crossed a pin comment's bound, none is in the `.github/dependabot.yml` ignore list, and there are no majors.

## Evidence

**ddtrace** is the one with teeth. `utils/logutil.py:163` walks the private `cur._parent` attribute to tag every span up to the service boundary, and a private attribute changing is exactly the kind of thing that fragments traces without raising anything. Diffing the two wheels, `ddtrace/_trace/` and `ddtrace/trace/` are byte-identical between the two versions, as are the Flask, Celery, requests and botocore instrumentation packages. Asserted directly under 4.14.1 that `child._parent is parent` holds, that it returns a `Span`, and that the walk stops when the service changes; the three guards in `test/utils/logutil_test.py` (`test_span_parent_returns_the_parent_span`, `test_local_span_chain_returns_current_then_same_service_parents`, `test_local_span_chain_stops_at_a_different_service`) pass. The Python files that did change are the LLM-observability contribs (google_adk, google_genai, mcp, vllm), `llmobs/`, the CI-visibility helpers, and one guard in `internal/settings/profiling.py` that turns off fast memory copy for stack profiling under an embedded interpreter. None of those preconditions are met here: there is no LLMObs reference anywhere in the repo, and `config.py:545` sets `DD_PROFILING_ENABLED` to false.

**urllib3** is a meaty release, but the only place we construct anything from it is `utils/utils.py:581`, `Retry(total=total, backoff_factor=backoff_factor)`. Both of those fields are untouched in `util/retry.py`; the only behavior change there is a new `FutureWarning` that fires when `allowed_methods` is passed as an empty collection, and we pass neither `allowed_methods` nor `status_forcelist`. Read the rest of the changed modules for anything reaching us through requests: `util/ssl_.py` only wraps a bad fingerprint string in `SSLError` instead of letting `binascii.Error` escape, with no change to TLS version or cipher defaults; `response.py` bounds the chunk-size line length while streaming and fixes deflate handling after EOF; `connection.py` collapses obsolete folded header values; `connectionpool.py` and `poolmanager.py` strip the URL fragment before sending and clear the chunked framing when a redirect drops the body. All correctness fixes, none of which changes the shape of what a vendor call gets back. The other changed modules (`contrib/pyopenssl.py`, `contrib/socks.py`, `http2/connection.py`) are not on any path we use.

**datadog-cdk-constructs-v2** rewrote how a Lambda layer ARN is built: 5.1.0 appended `-ARM` to a per-runtime base name, 5.2.0 looks the name up in a new `layer-runtime-catalog.js` keyed by architecture. For python3.12, which is what `templates/cluster.py:282` gives the proxy function, the catalog returns `Datadog-Python312` for x86_64, the same string the old code produced. Confirmed it end to end: synthesized all 32 templates on `origin/main` and again on this branch, compared each pair as JSON with sorted keys, and none of the 32 differ. No logical ID moved and no resource would be replaced on deploy. The props `templates/cluster.py:309` passes to `DatadogLambda` are all still accepted, and the construct's own class is unchanged apart from its version string.

**awslambdaric** is two lines. `__init__.py` bumps `__version__`, and `bootstrap.py` renames one key in the JSON it logs on a handler error from `log_level` to `level`. Nothing in this repo reads either key, and `python -m awslambdaric` (the container entrypoint set at `templates/lambda_services.py:125`) still resolves in 4.0.4. The runtime API contract itself is untouched.

`yarn test nonints`: 829 passed. The three logutil guards named above pass, and `yarn synth -s dev` renders all 32 templates identically before and after.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/harshanandiwada/workspace/pokedex/.claude/skills/claudish-output

# claudish-output

The claudish display hook (`.claude/hooks/claudish/`) rewrites what the user reads in chat and never touches text that is sent somewhere else. This skill runs the prose of an outgoing artifact through the same rewrite prompts and the same provider layer, with the house rules in `.claude/rules/communications.md` added, so the reader on the other end gets plain language in the repo's own voice. Claude Haiku does the rewrite by default, through the Claude Code binary of the running session, so the result is the same on a laptop and in a cloud session and no local model is needed.

The script is `.claude/skills/claudish-output/rewrite-text.sh`, run from the repo root with `bash`.

## Steps

1. Draft the text as usual, under `.claude/rules/communications.md` for its surface (PR, Linear, Slack, email). Give a PR body its lead line before rewriting; the rewriter keeps structure, it does not add it.
2. Separate what must not be rewritten: PR template sections (checklist, the `test override:` line, the ship-on-merge block), fenced or machine-read blocks, raw URLs, identifiers. Save each piece of prose to its own scratchpad file. A title is its own file.
3. Rewrite each file, naming what it is:
   ```bash
   bash .claude/skills/claudish-output/rewrite-text.sh --surface "<what the text is>" [--title] [--style plain|tldr|5y|caveman|configured] [--provider claude|ollama|anthropic|openai|codex|auto] <file>
   ```
   - `--surface`: what the text is, in words: "PR body", "PR title", "Linear card body", "Slack reply to a customer", "vendor support email", "commit message". The rules give each surface its own length ceiling and tone, and the rewriter can only apply them when it knows which one it is holding.
   - `--title`: one line in, one line out, keeping an `area: ` or `[TRA-1234]` prefix when the input has one. The script exits 1 if that prefix is missing from the output, the surest sign the model answered the title instead of rewriting it.
   - `--style plain` (default) is the only style for text another person receives: the base prompt plus the whole of `communications.md`, applied as an edit pass. A sentence changes only where it breaks a rule (an em-dash, filler, jargon, a sentence that needs two reads); the rest stays as written, nothing is summarized or merged, and every identifier the author wrote survives. The text reaches the model as data inside `<text>` tags, so a draft that reads like a request is still rewritten rather than answered. The other styles are display styles for the reader's own screen and skip the rules. `configured` copies the chat display style, which is a half-length summary (`tldr`) unless `/claudish style` changed it, so use it only when the user names it, never for something being sent.
   - `--provider claude` (default) is Haiku through `claude -p`. `auto` uses the display hook's provider (`CLAUDISH_PROVIDER`, with its `CLAUDISH_MODEL` and `~/.claude/claudish-repo-model`) and falls back to `claude` when that returns nothing; a provider named explicitly fails instead of switching, since it was chosen for where the text is allowed to go. The script names the provider it used on stderr; repeat that to the user in one line.
4. Read the output against the draft: every identifier, number, link and file path present; nothing invented; markdown intact; each bullet still says what the draft said. Fix a drift by hand in the output rather than re-running, and tell the user what you fixed.
5. Reassemble with the untouched parts and send.

## Showing the rewrite in chat

When the claudish display hook is on, it shows a summary in place of every chat message. A message that shows this rewrite would reach the user as a summary of a rewrite, and a draft they copy out of chat would be that summary, not the text. The script says on stderr when the hook is on. Then the message that shows the rewrite starts with this line, as its very first line, before any other word:

```
<!-- claudish:original -->
```

The hook leaves a message that begins with that marker as written and strips the marker from view; `/claudish last` uses the same one. The marker goes on the chat message only, never into the artifact being sent.

## When the script exits 1

No rewrite came back; the message names the provider and the error. Do not send the draft as if it were the rewrite. Tell the user and ask whether to send the draft unchanged.

## Requirements

- `claude` (default): the Claude Code running the session (`CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH`, else `claude` on PATH), signed in. The call runs with no tools, no setting sources, a replaced system prompt, and a temp working directory, so no project instructions, plugins, or hooks shape the rewrite. It takes 10 to 60 seconds per piece and counts against the account's usage.
- `.claude/rules/communications.md`, read at run time for the plain style (`CLAUDISH_RULES_FILE` points elsewhere). The script exits 1 without it rather than rewriting to the generic prompt alone.
- Any other provider: whatever `.claude/hooks/claudish/providers.sh` documents for it (ollama running with the model pulled, an API key in the environment, the codex CLI). `CLAUDISH_TIMEOUT` bounds the call (default 120 s here).

content.content:
**ddtrace** is the one with teeth. `utils/logutil.py:163` walks the private `cur._parent` attribute to tag every span up to the service boundary, and a private attribute changing is exactly the kind of thing that fragments traces without raising anything. Diffing the two wheels, `ddtrace/_trace/` and `ddtrace/trace/` are byte-identical between the two versions, as are the Flask, Celery, requests and botocore instrumentation packages. Asserted directly under 4.14.1 that `child._parent is parent` holds, that it returns a `Span`, and that the walk stops when the service changes; the three guards in `test/utils/logutil_test.py` (`test_span_parent_returns_the_parent_span`, `test_local_span_chain_returns_current_then_same_service_parents`, `test_local_span_chain_stops_at_a_different_service`) pass. The Python files that did change are the LLM-observability contribs (google_adk, google_genai, mcp, vllm), `llmobs/`, the CI-visibility helpers, and one guard in `internal/settings/profiling.py` that turns off fast memory copy for stack profiling under an embedded interpreter. None of those preconditions are met here: there is no LLMObs reference anywhere in the repo, and `config.py:545` sets `DD_PROFILING_ENABLED` to false.

**urllib3** is a meaty release, but the only place we construct anything from it is `utils/utils.py:581`, `Retry(total=total, backoff_factor=backoff_factor)`. Both of those fields are untouched in `util/retry.py`; the only behavior change there is a new `FutureWarning` that fires when `allowed_methods` is passed as an empty collection, and we pass neither `allowed_methods` nor `status_forcelist`. Read the rest of the changed modules for anything reaching us through requests: `util/ssl_.py` only wraps a bad fingerprint string in `SSLError` instead of letting `binascii.Error` escape, with no change to TLS version or cipher defaults; `response.py` bounds the chunk-size line length while streaming and fixes deflate handling after EOF; `connection.py` collapses obsolete folded header values; `connectionpool.py` and `poolmanager.py` strip the URL fragment before sending and clear the chunked framing when a redirect drops the body. All correctness fixes, none of which changes the shape of what a vendor call gets back. The other changed modules (`contrib/pyopenssl.py`, `contrib/socks.py`, `http2/connection.py`) are not on any path we use.

**datadog-cdk-constructs-v2** rewrote how a Lambda layer ARN is built: 5.1.0 appended `-ARM` to a per-runtime base name, 5.2.0 looks the name up in a new `layer-runtime-catalog.js` keyed by architecture. For python3.12, which is what `templates/cluster.py:282` gives the proxy function, the catalog returns `Datadog-Python312` for x86_64, the same string the old code produced. Confirmed it end to end: synthesized all 32 templates on `origin/main` and again on this branch, compared each pair as JSON with sorted keys, and none of the 32 differ. No logical ID moved and no resource would be replaced on deploy. The props `templates/cluster.py:309` passes to `DatadogLambda` are all still accepted, and the construct's own class is unchanged apart from its version string.

**awslambdaric** is two lines. `__init__.py` bumps `__version__`, and `bootstrap.py` renames one key in the JSON it logs on a handler error from `log_level` to `level`. Nothing in this repo reads either key, and `python -m awslambdaric` (the container entrypoint set at `templates/lambda_services.py:125`) still works. The runtime API contract itself is untouched.

## Verification

`yarn test nonints`: 829 passed. The three logutil guards named above pass, and `yarn synth -s dev` renders all 32 templates identically before and after.

One new bump since yesterday: **aws-cdk-lib 2.269.0 → 2.270.0** (#6151). Vetted clean and folded onto #6123, which is now five packages: https://github.com/trackstarhq/pokedex/pull/6123

`main` had moved (#6155 landed), so I merged it into the host branch before adding the bump.

**aws-cdk-lib evidence.** It's in the ignore list for patches only, and this is a minor, so it's allowed through. 20 modules changed; three of them are ones `templates/` imports — `aws_ecs`, `aws_lambda`, `aws_s3`. All three are docstring edits plus one additive class (`DirectS3Read` in `aws_lambda`); nothing removed or renamed. The `aws_ecs` change is a doc correction about `enable_managed_draining`, which we never set.

The synth check is the part worth reading: **all 32 templates differ**, but every one differs on exactly one line — the `Analytics` property of the `AWS::CDK::Metadata` resource, which is CDK's own gzipped inventory of the constructs a stack uses. I decoded both sides of all 32: the construct inventory is byte-identical and only the version prefix moves (`2.269.0!` → `2.270.0!`). Re-diffing with that one property excluded gives 0 of 32 differing, so no logical ID moved and nothing would be replaced on deploy.

`uv.lock` moved only the five bumped packages plus jsii 1.139.0→1.140.0 (datadog-cdk's transitive); aws-cdk-lib pulled in nothing new. `yarn test nonints`: 829 passed.

Superseded, for a human to close once #6123 merges: **#6124, #6125, #6126, #6151**. Still not merged, no ship box ticked. Local checkout is back on clean `main`.

19:`uv.lock` also moves jsii 1.139.0 -> 1.140.0, which datadog-cdk-constructs-v2 5.2.0 requires. ddtrace 4.15.1 brings its own two new entries, ddtrace-internal 0.1.0 and a second bytecode (0.19.0). Nothing else moved; aws-cdk-lib 2.270.0 pulls in nothing new.
25:**ddtrace** is the one with teeth, and it now goes 4.14.0 -> 4.15.1, a minor rather than the patch Dependabot originally opened. `utils/logutil.py:163` walks the private `cur._parent` attribute to tag every span up to the service boundary. Version 4.15 rewrites `_trace/span.py`, removing `_local_root`, `_service_entry_span` and `_is_top_level` from `Span` and trimming `__slots__` down to five entries. `_parent` itself survives at `span.py:126`, and ddtrace's own walk at `span.py:580` still follows it. We do not touch any of the three removed names. Asserted directly under 4.15.1 that `child._parent is parent` holds, that it returns a `Span`, that `current_root_span()` still returns a `Span` (`logutil.py:142` calls it), and that the walk stops when the service changes. The three guards in `test/utils/logutil_test.py` pass: `test_span_parent_returns_the_parent_span`, `test_local_span_chain_returns_current_then_same_service_parents`, and `test_local_span_chain_stops_at_a_different_service`.
27:On the instrumentation side, the Flask and Celery packages are byte-identical across the two versions. The requests package changes only where it reads the APM opt-out setting and drops two eager `Pin(...).onto(...)` calls at import, neither of which we use. The botocore package is comment cleanup plus one real change in `utils.py`: on the EventBridge produce path it now passes the request params and entry through to the data-streams handler instead of `None`, but only when data streams is enabled. That flag is enabled here, `templates/cluster_services.py:60` sets `DD_DATA_STREAMS_ENABLED` to true on the cluster services, so the second condition is what settles it: the path needs a botocore `PutEvents` call, and there is none in the repo. Our EventBridge use is SP-API subscribing us as a destination, never publishing to it.

lines: - `order.additional_fields.customer_message` / `additional_fields.staff_notes` ← v2 order `customer_message` / `staff_notes`, passed through raw (empty string preserved, no `or None`).

- Customer-requested (Pylon 5715): the "order notes" a merchant sees in the BigCommerce order UI are these two fields — verified live on order `109`, whose `customer_message` matches the note in the customer's screenshot. The canonical cart order schema has no notes slot, so `additional_fields` is the correct carrier; Shopify sets the precedent with `additional_fields.note` as a raw pass-through.

-- `order.status`: `"Completed"` (status_id 10) maps to `fulfilled` EXCEPT when the store renamed the label (`custom_status != status`) and the order is physical (`order_is_digital` false) — then `confirmed`.

+- `order.status` is derived from the numeric `status_id` (0-14, fixed platform-wide), not the `status` label, which merchants can rename in the BigCommerce admin (TRA-2652). The `Incomplete` skip in `get_orders` and the post-shipment status wait key on the id for the same reason.
+- `status_id` 10 (`Completed`) maps to `fulfilled` EXCEPT when the store renamed the label (`custom_status != status`) and the order is physical (`order_is_digital` false) — then `confirmed`.

- BigCommerce's stock meaning of status 10 is the digital-goods done state ("file(s) available for download"); physical-goods merchants who use it at all have repurposed it. The rename is the observable signal of repurposing: a fleet sweep of all 14 active connections (2026-08-19, Pylon 5755) found exactly 3 renamed it — Luminous org's `e6ecfa0d…`/`232c068a…` (same store) and `b6c48332…`, all to "Received", all using it as a pre-shipment intake state (orders later move to Shipped; sampled status-10 orders show `items_shipped: 0`). All 11 standard-label connections keep the stock mapping, unchanged.

- `items_shipped` was rejected as the signal: standard stores routinely complete physical orders without recording BigCommerce shipments (`9adb0f43…` all 12.5k Completed orders are 0-shipped physical; `cd551521…` recent Completed same), so shipment-count logic would flip genuinely-done orders to not-fulfilled. `date_shipped` is also useless — stamped on entry to status 10 even with zero shipments.
- The `order_is_digital` guard keeps auto-completed digital purchases `fulfilled` even on renamed stores (observed: 2 digital orders in `e6ecfa0d…`'s "Received" status, genuinely delivered).

+            # skip "Incomplete" orders - abandoned carts, not fulfillable

# digital orders auto-complete into it and really are done
# read the status through the same map format_order uses, so the wait ends

Good catch. There is — **4.15.1**, and there's no PR for it. That comment is Dependabot saying it stopped maintaining this branch once I pushed to it, so it won't update #6123 or open a separate ddtrace PR until this merges. I picked 4.15.1 up off PyPI and vetted it by hand; #6123 now carries it.

It's a **minor**, not the patch I vetted first, and it genuinely rewrites `_trace/span.py` — so this needed a real second pass rather than a rubber stamp:

- **Removals in `Span`:** 4.15 drops `_local_root`, `_service_entry_span` and `_is_top_level`, and trims `__slots__` to five entries. We use none of those three. `_parent` survives at `span.py:126`, and ddtrace's own walk at `span.py:580` still follows it.
- **Asserted under 4.15.1:** `child._parent is parent`, returns a `Span`, `current_root_span()` still returns a `Span` (`logutil.py:142` calls it), walk stops at the service boundary. The three `logutil_test.py` guards pass.
- **Instrumentation:** Flask and Celery byte-identical. `requests` only moves where it reads the APM opt-out setting and drops two eager `Pin(...).onto(...)` calls we don't use.
- **The one that needed chasing:** `botocore/utils.py` now passes the request params and entry to the data-streams handler on the EventBridge produce path, gated on data streams being enabled — and it *is* enabled, `templates/cluster_services.py:60` sets `DD_DATA_STREAMS_ENABLED=true` on the cluster services. What settles it is the second condition: that path needs a botocore `PutEvents` call and there is none in the repo. Our EventBridge use is SP-API subscribing us as a destination, never publishing.

`uv.lock` gains two entries from 4.15.1 — `ddtrace-internal 0.1.0` and a second `bytecode` (0.19.0) — both noted in the body. `yarn test nonints`: 829 passed. Re-synthed: 0 of 32 templates move.

Six packages now on https://github.com/trackstarhq/pokedex/pull/6123. Still unmerged, no ship box ticked, local checkout back on clean `main`.
